title: Implement industry-standard Pinata directory upload workflow (images CID + per-token metadata CID) with asset locking

requirements.text: Update the IPFS/Pinata upload workflow to exactly follow: (1) upload the entire images folder as a single directory upload and receive IMAGES_FOLDER_CID; (2) generate one metadata JSON file per token with an `image` field set to `ipfs://IMAGES_FOLDER_CID/<TOKEN_ID>.png`; (3) upload the entire metadata folder as a single directory upload and receive METADATA_FOLDER_CID; and (4) present the final token URI format as `ipfs://METADATA_FOLDER_CID/<TOKEN_ID>.json`.

quotes: workflow for uploading to IPFS without changing any existing features or the current app layout ... Upload images folder only → receive IMAGES_FOLDER_CID ... Upload metadata folder only → receive METADATA_FOLDER_CID

acceptanceCriteria: Running the app’s Upload action results in TWO Pinata uploads: one for images (directory) and one for metadata (directory).
The images upload returns a CID used in metadata `image` fields as `ipfs://IMAGES_FOLDER_CID/<TOKEN_ID>.png` (no extra subfolder segment like `/images/`).
The metadata upload returns a CID such that token URIs are `ipfs://METADATA_FOLDER_CID/<TOKEN_ID>.json`.
The app no longer uploads a single merged metadata JSON (e.g., `MONKE_INDEX_metadata.json`) to Pinata as the primary metadata output.

requirements.text: Fix Pinata directory upload construction so directory uploads cannot collapse/merge metadata into a single file: ensure every file appended to `FormData` for directory uploads includes the intended per-file path/name (via the third parameter of `formData.append('file', blob, <path>)`) and that metadata is uploaded as multiple files (`1.json`, `2.json`, …) inside one directory upload.

quotes: the metadata uploaded to Pinata is being merged into a single file
Each NFT must have one JSON file: 1.json, 2.json, …

acceptanceCriteria: Pinata receives multiple multipart `file` parts for metadata (one per token) rather than one aggregated JSON payload.
The resulting IPFS content for METADATA_FOLDER_CID contains individual files `1.json`, `2.json`, … (not a single `*_metadata.json`).
Each metadata file contains an `image` field pointing to the corresponding token image IPFS URI.

requirements.text: Enforce 1-based sequential filenames for both exported assets and Pinata uploads: images must be named `1.png`, `2.png`, `3.png`, … and metadata files must be `1.json`, `2.json`, `3.json`, … (no `0.png`/`0.json` in the IPFS upload workflow).

quotes: Each NFT must have one JSON file: 1.json, 2.json, …

acceptanceCriteria: The images directory upload contains files named exactly `1.png..N.png`.
The metadata directory upload contains files named exactly `1.json..N.json`.
The `<TOKEN_ID>` used in both `ipfs://IMAGES_FOLDER_CID/<TOKEN_ID>.png` and `ipfs://METADATA_FOLDER_CID/<TOKEN_ID>.json` matches this 1-based numbering.

requirements.text: Implement final asset locking behavior: when the collection is locked for publishing, disable the Vault "Generate" action (and any regeneration actions that would change the collection) and only re-enable them after the collection is unlocked, without changing the current app layout.

quotes: After locking the collection to prepare for uploading to Pinata, the Generate button should be disabled and only become clickable again after the collection is unlocked.

acceptanceCriteria: When `project.collectionLocked` is true, the Generate button in the Vault cannot be clicked and does not trigger generation.
When the collection is unlocked, the Generate button returns to its prior enabled behavior.
No new pages or major layout rearrangements are introduced; the existing Vault layout remains intact.

requirements.text: Ensure exported images match the exact pixel dimensions configured in the Settings section for the project, and that the same sizing is used for the images that are uploaded to Pinata (so all assets in the uploaded images folder share identical dimensions).

quotes: Export the entire collection as PNG or JPG, Ensure all assets have the same size and match the exact dimensions (px) configured in the Settings section.

acceptanceCriteria: All generated/exported images use the project’s configured output dimensions (per Settings) rather than a hard-coded size.
All uploaded images in the Pinata images directory share identical width/height matching Settings.
If Settings output size is changed and the collection is regenerated, newly exported/uploaded images reflect the updated dimensions.

requirements.text: Keep the existing upload controls flow (Lock → Upload → Unlock) but update status/output text to clearly show both returned CIDs (IMAGES_FOLDER_CID and METADATA_FOLDER_CID) and the final token URI format `ipfs://METADATA_FOLDER_CID/<TOKEN_ID>.json`, using English for all user-facing text.

quotes: Receive a single folder CID: IMAGES_FOLDER_CID
Receive a metadata folder CID: METADATA_FOLDER_CID
Use English for any user-facing text in the build request.

acceptanceCriteria: After a successful upload, the UI displays the metadata folder CID and the images folder CID (or otherwise makes both accessible to the user).
The UI shows the final token URI pattern exactly as `ipfs://METADATA_FOLDER_CID/<TOKEN_ID>.json`.
All newly introduced/modified user-facing strings are in English.

constraints: Do not change any existing features outside the IPFS/Pinata publishing workflow.
Do not change the current app layout (no major UI restructuring).

Frontend immutable paths must not be edited: frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, frontend/src/components/ui.
Backend must remain single-actor; avoid backend changes unless strictly required (this workflow should be frontend-only).
nonGoals: Adding new third-party auth providers (only Internet Identity is supported).
Adding real-time features (WebSockets, live progress via sockets, etc.).
Introducing external databases or non-IC backend services.
Changing how NFTs are generated artistically beyond enforcing output dimensions and locking behavior.
